name: Power distribution block
summary: A terminal assembly that splits one incoming conductor into several outgoing conductors on a common bar.
description: A power distribution block takes one large incoming conductor and distributes it to several smaller outgoing conductors on a shared conducting bar, saving space compared with stacking lugs on one terminal. It is used in control panels to distribute supply to several circuit breakers or loads.

The symbol shows the shared node and terminal count but not the short-circuit current rating, which varies widely between products and must suit the available fault current. Outgoing conductors connected to a distribution block usually need upstream protection sized for the smallest outgoing conductor unless tap rules allow otherwise.
readingNotes: Check the block's short-circuit current rating against the panel rating.
drawingChecklist: State block current and short-circuit rating.
distinction: A power distribution block is one node with many terminals; a multi-conductor terminal block is a single terminal accepting several wires.
